column3:
The fundamental economic problem where unlimited wants exceed limited resources.
What is opportunity cost?"
column4:
The value of the next best alternative foregone when a choice is made.
Define factors of production."
column5:
Land, labour, capital, and enterprise.
What is productive efficiency?"
column6:
When output is produced at the lowest possible cost per unit.
What is allocative efficiency?"
column7:
When resources are allocated to produce the goods and services most desired by consumers (P = MC).
What is dynamic efficiency?"
column8:
Efficiency achieved over time through innovation and investment.
What is a production possibility frontier (PPF)?"
column9:
A curve showing the maximum possible output combinations of two goods given resources and technology.
What causes an outward shift of the PPF?"
column10:
Increase in quantity/quality of resources or improvements in technology.
Define specialisation."
column11:
Concentrating on producing a limited range of goods to increase efficiency.
What is the law of diminishing returns?"
column12:
Adding more of a variable factor to a fixed factor eventually leads to smaller increases in output.
What is demand?"
column13:
The willingness and ability to pay for a good at a given price over a period of time.
State the law of demand."
column14:
As price falls, quantity demanded rises, ceteris paribus.
List determinants of demand."
column15:
Income, tastes, price of related goods, population, advertising, expectations.
What is price elasticity of demand (PED)?"
column16:
Measure of responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price.\nPED = %ΔQd / %ΔP
When is demand price elastic?"
column17:
When PED > 1 (quantity demanded changes more than price).
What is income elasticity of demand (YED)?"
column18:
Measure of responsiveness of demand to a change in income.\nYED = %ΔQd / %ΔY
What is a normal good?"
column19:
A good with positive income elasticity of demand (YED > 0).
What is an inferior good?"
column20:
A good with negative income elasticity of demand (YED < 0).
What is cross elasticity of demand (XED)?"
column21:
Measure of responsiveness of demand for one good to a change in price of another.\nXED = %ΔQd(A) / %ΔP(B)
What is supply?"
column22:
The willingness and ability to produce and sell a good at a given price over a period of time.
State the law of supply."
column23:
As price rises, quantity supplied rises, ceteris paribus.
List determinants of supply."
column24:
Costs of production, technology, taxes/subsidies, number of firms, expectations.
What is price elasticity of supply (PES)?"
column25:
Measure of responsiveness of quantity supplied to a change in price.\nPES = %ΔQs / %ΔP
When is supply perfectly inelastic?"
column26:
When PES = 0 and the supply curve is vertical.
Define market equilibrium."
column27:
The price where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied.
What is consumer surplus?"
column28:
The difference between what consumers are willing to pay and what they actually pay.
What is producer surplus?"
column29:
The difference between the price producers receive and their minimum acceptable price.
What is a subsidy?"
column30:
A government payment to producers to encourage production or consumption.
What is an indirect tax?"
column31:
A tax imposed on spending on goods and services (e.g. VAT).
What is a maximum price (price ceiling)?"
column32:
A legal maximum price set below equilibrium, potentially causing excess demand.
What is a minimum price (price floor)?"
column33:
A legal minimum price set above equilibrium, potentially causing excess supply.
What is market failure?"
column34:
When the free market fails to allocate resources efficiently.
What are externalities?"
column35:
Third-party effects from production or consumption not reflected in market prices.
Define negative externality of production."
column36:
When production imposes external costs on third parties.
Define positive externality of consumption."
column37:
When consumption provides external benefits to third parties.
What is social cost?"
column38:
Private cost + external cost.
What is social benefit?"
column39:
Private benefit + external benefit.
What is a public good?"
column40:
A good that is non-rival and non-excludable.
What is the free rider problem?"
column41:
When individuals benefit from a good without paying for it.
Define merit good."
column42:
A good under-consumed in a free market due to information failure.
Define demerit good."
column43:
A good over-consumed in a free market due to information failure.
What is asymmetric information?"
column44:
When one party in a transaction has more information than the other.
What is moral hazard?"
column45:
When one party takes more risks because they do not bear the full consequences.
What is adverse selection?"
column46:
When asymmetric information leads to the wrong participants entering a market.
What is a monopoly?"
column47:
A market structure with one dominant firm and high barriers to entry.
State one barrier to entry."
column48:
Economies of scale.
What is monopolistic competition?"
column49:
A market structure with many firms selling differentiated products and low barriers to entry.
What is an oligopoly?"
column50:
A market structure dominated by a few large firms with interdependence.
What is collusion?"
column51:
When firms cooperate to limit competition, often by fixing prices.
What is price discrimination?"
column52:
Charging different prices to different consumers for the same product.
What is economic profit?"
column53:
Revenue minus total costs (including normal profit).
What is normal profit?"
column54:
The minimum reward needed to keep a firm in its current use.
What is marginal cost?"
column55:
The cost of producing one extra unit of output.
What is marginal revenue?"
column56:
The additional revenue gained from selling one more unit.
What is the profit maximisation rule?"
column57:
A firm maximises profit where MR = MC.
